criteria.name: Mission concept and rationale — What will it do, who are the users, why is it needed?
criteria.reasoning: Clear, well-motivated concept: purpose (bleach detection, SST, thermal stress, bathymetry), users (marine/conservation scientists), and Australian benefit are explicit, with literature cited. However, no quantified mission requirements (resolution, revisit, coverage, orbit) are stated, so it sits at the lower end of Accomplished.

evidence.quote: A near-real-time relay to monitoring stations on the ground would allow marine and conservation scientists to more accurately predict and react to coral bleaching events.
In 2016, a bleaching killed 30 percent of the reef’s coral. In 2017, another 20 percent perished.

criteria.name: Project plan — How you plan to complete the assignment, including either a Gantt chart or a timetable and information sources you plan to use
criteria.reasoning: Gantt chart with colour-coded progress, deadlines and per-task descriptions tied to the mission (launch, orbit, ground control, comms, EOL, STK). Week 10 review acts as a buffer, but no explicit contingency or risk provision is stated, and some task sequencing is questionable.

evidence.quote: Project work will be divided into weeks via a Gantt Chart. Detailed task descriptions can be found on the next page.
The syllabus work on astrodynamics will help me to understand and design an optimal mission.

criteria.name: Preliminary progress — Technical content and evidence of sufficient work done to date
criteria.reasoning: Progress to date is limited to background reading and four STK tutorials; no orbit, launch, link-budget or simulation results are presented or interpreted. This is minor work only, though it is consistent with being on track.

criteria.name: Report presentation
criteria.reasoning: Logical structure, clear readable prose, consistent formatting, superscript citations matching the source list. Deductions: the Gantt lacks a numbered figure caption, and the reference list is bare URLs without titles or access dates.

evidence.quote: Completed stages are gold. Incomplete stages are blue. Deadlines are indicated by red lines.

technical_issues.issue: STK Simulations (Wk 4–10) is scheduled to start before STK Design (Wk 7–9), an illogical task dependency.
Background Research runs to Wk 8 while Mission Concept is marked complete in Wk 3, leaving the concept unsupported by later research.
No quantified mission requirements (ground resolution, revisit time, spectral bands, coverage, lifetime) are defined to drive the design.
'Oceans have become 30 percent more acidic' is imprecise; the commonly cited figure is a ~30% rise in hydrogen-ion concentration (pH drop ~0.1).
No contingency, risk, or mitigation is described for schedule slippage or STK/software access problems.
STK is named but not justified against alternatives, and no software outputs are shown.

overall: Strong, well-referenced mission concept and a clear Gantt-based plan tied to the space segment. Technical progress is thin—only tutorials and reading—and requirements remain unquantified. Presentation is professional with minor referencing and figure-caption weaknesses.

feedback.summary: Your mission concept is clear and well-referenced, and your Gantt-based plan is tied to the space segment. To move higher, quantify requirements, add contingency/risk, justify STK, and show technical results. Presentation is professional; add a numbered Gantt caption and full reference details.
next_steps: Add quantified mission requirements (ground resolution, revisit time, spectral bands, coverage, lifetime) to Mission Concept & Rationale and link each to a user need.
Revise the Gantt in Image 1: fix the STK Simulations/Design dependency and Background Research timing; add explicit contingency/risk rows and a short STK justification.
Produce at least one preliminary technical result (e.g., orbit or link-budget output) with brief interpretation, and add a numbered caption to the Gantt plus full reference entries.

criteria.C1: You clearly explain the mission purpose, users and Australian benefit, with good literature support. To reach the top of Accomplished, add quantified requirements—ground resolution, revisit time, spectral bands, coverage and lifetime—and tie each to a user need. Also correct the ocean-acidity statement to specify the ~30% rise in hydrogen-ion concentration (pH drop ~0.1).
criteria.C2: Your colour-coded Gantt and task descriptions make the plan credible and mission-linked. Next level requires explicit contingency/risk provision and a justified software choice. Fix Image 1 sequencing: STK Simulations (Wk 4–10) should not start before STK Design (Wk 7–9), and Background Research running to Wk 8 conflicts with Mission Concept completing in Wk 3.
criteria.C3: You have completed STK tutorials 1–4 and background reading, which shows a start. To move from Adequate, present at least one preliminary technical result—orbit, launch, link-budget or simulation output—with a brief description and interpretation, and show how it feeds the design.
criteria.C4: Your report is logically structured, readable and consistently formatted, with superscript citations matching the source list. To secure the top of Accomplished, add a numbered caption to the Gantt in Image 1 and expand the reference list from bare URLs to full entries with titles and access dates.
